features.summary: Firefox’s CSS style system became more consistent and robust, with many properties moved to shared predefined representations and better handling of computed colors, variation settings, CSSOM exposure, and pref-controlled features. It also fixes edge cases involving CSS zoom, text boxes, fieldsets, blending, masks, and scrolling, while adding the `grid-lanes` value for `display` and recognizing `plus-lighter` for `background-blend-mode`. _Most of this is behind-the-scenes work that improves correctness and maintainability, rather than a visible redesign._

features.summary: Layout and reflow were hardened against invalid frame-tree states, weak references, and tricky positioning cases, including sticky positioning, SVG text, absolute-positioned content, and nested iframe printing. Firefox also improved caret placement after paragraph-ending newlines, SVG intrinsic sizing, scroll snapping, automatic line clamping, and restoration of scroll positions without emitting misleading scroll events. **These changes make complex pages more stable and predictable as content is laid out, resized, printed, or restored.**

It also separated history-based scroll restoration from frame-based state restoration and moved more restoration logic into scroll containers, while updating internal APIs and input-test setup. _These are largely foundational changes that support more reliable positioning and page restoration._

features.summary: The reftest suite was updated to more accurately validate WebRender rendering, including visible-region image sampling, pixel snapping, image raster sizes, capture rotation, and flattened 3D transforms. Tests for XSLT, dynamic toolbars, and other pref-controlled behavior were corrected or re-enabled, with fuzziness adjusted where rendering differences are expected. **The result is more trustworthy visual testing and fewer false failures for graphics-heavy pages.**

features.summary: Firefox improved SVG bounding-box calculations for `tspan` and `textPath` elements, including support for their `getBBox()` options and more centralized handling of their geometry. It now also avoids calculating a bounding box when a non-scaling-stroke transform is singular, preventing invalid or unusable results. _These changes improve the accuracy and safety of SVG text measurement and rendering._

patches.subject: Carry the display list normalization offset in i64

features.summary: Display-list painting now represents gradient geometry with vectors and carries normalization offsets using 64-bit values. This improves precision for gradients and for content positioned at very large or unusual coordinates, reducing the risk of rendering errors. _There is no intended visible change for ordinary pages._

features.summary: Firefox removed the old `NS_PRINTING` build option and the `--disable-printing` command-line switch, making printing support a standard part of the browser build. Documentation was also clarified so contributors know how Web Platform Tests (WPTs) should be handled in the layout code. **Printing can no longer be selectively compiled out through that legacy setting.**

features.label: XUL layout

features.summary: XUL popup rendering was streamlined by using a more suitable segmented data structure, and popup placement on Wayland now shares the same right-to-left anchor-flipping logic used elsewhere. This helps menus and other XUL popups use consistent positioning, especially for RTL interfaces and Linux’s Wayland display system. _The changes mainly improve internal consistency and platform reliability._

features.label: Build

patches.author: Tom Schuster
patches.subject: Add ConnectionAllowlistsService stub.

features.summary: The build gained a stub for the ConnectionAllowlistsService, allowing code that depends on that service interface to compile or run in configurations where the full service is not present. This is infrastructure work rather than a user-facing feature. _No visible browser behavior is intended to change._

features.label: MathML

patches.author: tannal
patches.subject: Avoid integer overflow when layouting mpadded using voffset or lspace.

features.summary: MathML layout now guards against integer overflow when `mpadded` uses `voffset` or `lspace` values. This prevents extreme or malformed mathematical markup from producing incorrect dimensions or destabilizing layout. **MathML pages are safer and more predictable when padding offsets are unusually large.**

features.label: Media IPC

patches.author: Hiroyuki Ikezoe
patches.subject: Track each pipeline's embedder LayersId in CompositorBridgeParent::LayerTreeState.

features.summary: Media IPC now records the compositor `LayersId` associated with each media pipeline’s embedder. This gives Firefox’s media and graphics processes the tracking information needed to associate video layers with the correct compositor tree, improving reliability for rendered media.

features.label: Other

patches.author: Mark Banner
patches.subject: Rename remaining browser/base/content/test browser-chrome directories to match eslint-test-paths conventions

features.summary: Remaining browser-chrome test directories were renamed to follow Firefox’s `eslint-test-paths` conventions. There is no user-visible change, but test discovery and linting are now more consistent.

features.label: Printing & print preview

patches.author: Emilio Cobos Álvarez
patches.subject: Remove MOZ_ENABLE_SKIA_PDF.

features.summary: Firefox removed the `MOZ_ENABLE_SKIA_PDF` build option, eliminating a legacy switch for selecting Skia PDF support. This simplifies the printing and print-preview build configuration while keeping printing itself available. _The change is primarily internal and should not alter normal print-preview use._

features.label: Style inspector APIs

patches.author: Nicolas Chevobbe
patches.subject: Fix CSSStyleRule#selectorMatchesElement for ::part() + nested shadow elements.

features.summary: The Style Inspector API method `CSSStyleRule#selectorMatchesElement` now correctly handles `::part()` selectors when they cross nested shadow DOM boundaries. This makes programmatic selector checks agree better with how CSS matches elements inside Web Components. **Developer tools and automation can now reliably inspect these encapsulated component styles.**

The work covers issues like non-scaling strokes, percentage-based sizing, and bounding boxes under font scaling, which is important for diagrams, maps, and responsive graphics. This makes SVG content appear more accurate and stable across different screen sizes and zoom levels.

features.summary: The browser’s XUL popups and menus were adjusted for more reliable positioning, especially on Wayland and with right-to-left layouts. These fixes improve tooltips, menus, and dropdowns so they anchor correctly, handle transparency more safely, and avoid crashes when native drag or popup state is missing. The changes are mostly under the hood, but they make classic browser UI feel more stable and predictable.

features.summary: The painting pipeline that builds display lists for the screen was hardened and simplified, especially around gradients, WebRender, and shadow corners. This reduces glitches where image layers, sticky content, or gradient fills could get mispainted or lose their visual shape. The result is more consistent graphics performance and fewer visual artifacts on complex pages and accelerated rendering setups.

These are foundation changes rather than user-facing features, but they make the browser leaner and its internal architecture more predictable. In short, it reduces maintenance burden and keeps the codebase closer to current standards.

This does not change the visible browser experience directly, but it makes the engineering pipeline more reliable and easier to maintain.

That means DevTools can show which styles actually apply to a component more reliably when page code uses web components and shadow roots. It does not change page rendering itself, but it makes debugging custom styling much more trustworthy.

features.summary: MathML layout now guards against integer overflow when `mpadded` uses `voffset` or `lspace` values. This prevents extreme or malformed mathematical markup from producing incorrect dimensions or destabilizing layout. **MathML pages are safer and more predictable when padding offsets are unusually large.**
